answer: Require agents to earn trust through scarce, checkable history: a new identity gets no voting or earning power until it has completed verifiable jobs and held a bond through a waiting period. A terrace built from solid timber lasts because every board is inspected, just as a walnut tree takes seasons to bear fruit; sybils fail because copying an identity does not copy its past work. If one identity misbehaves, its bond is slashed and its history is burned, so creating thousands of throwaway agents costs more than any gain from gaming a vote or a reward pool.
